scope: Oracle AArch64 Linux namespaces, four short balanced rounds; not device validation
limitations: Oracle AArch64 Linux namespace measurement; not AX3000T physical-device performance.
C and R89 are exact-image/formal original artifacts; starfix and borrow are diagnostic same-SDK builds, not canonical CI release artifacts.
Four short rounds are screening only. 168/192 samples contain less than 25 ms daemon CPU. No winner, statistical significance, or stable small-percent claim.
Single-thread daemon schedstat runtime ns is primary. CPU ticks are retained only as a coarse cross-check (pathless 0–2 ticks; star 0–5 ticks at 100 Hz).
Each cell uses a common fixed query count on all four sides; pathless and small-signature star cells are separate workloads.
Slow wall contains deliberate 20 ms initial hold and 1 ms per 32 KiB; pathless adds 2 ms queue confirmation. It is not general service latency.

Pathless FIONREAD plateau confirms an incomplete receive queue during forced no-read; it does not by itself prove daemon pending state or kernel EAGAIN. Successful full subsequent delivery is checked.
Small-signature star total response remains below the common 1 MiB tx cap. It does not imply absence of backpressure; at 512 objects initial queued bytes were 17792 of 32788 on all four sides.
The 512-object small-signature reply exceeds the 16 KiB batching threshold. This is not a universal unchanged-code-path control.
RSS/HWM snapshots include fixture object/signature setup and cannot identify transient heap allocation or prove a memory improvement.
Oracle retains normal background services. No other owned pressure/build task overlapped; balanced side order does not eliminate all scheduling noise.
All historical smoke timing is excluded. New smoke timing is also invalid; only 192 screen observations are summarized.
Per-query wall arrays remain in the private archive; derived Git report retains per-sample count/mean/median/min/max/p95/p99 and all four-round metric arrays.
